To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) training CNNs with stale weights is a viable approach to pipelined training of large CNNs, and (ii) a hybrid scheme combining pipelined training and non-pipelining training is a promising approach to address accuracy loss due to pipelining.
(1) pipelining the training of CNNs is possible without significant drop in inference accuracy, and (2) pipelining deeper in a network leads to a drop in accuracy.

(a) pipelined training with stale weights can converge to models with similar accuracies to those obtained with non-pipelined backpropagation when the pipelining is done early in the network and (b) when the pipelined back propagation is deep, the inference accuracy can drop significantly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How does the use of stale weight affect the statistical efficiency and inference accuracy of CNNs?
the impact of stale gradients in pipelined back-propagation.
the impact of stale gradients in the backpropagation of deep CNNs and the use of stale gradients in a pipelining scheme that maximizes utilization of accelerators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pipelining backpropagation with stale weights can significantly improve training throughput, with little impact on accuracy.
pipelined training with stale weights can be an effective technique for accelerating the training of CNNs on multiple accelerators.
we show that pipelined training of DNNs is possible with stale weights and can achieve speedup of up to 2X over non-pipelined baseline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pipelined back propagation with stale weights can be used in training CNNs to achieve speedups of 1.8-2X over a 4-GPU system with only a modest loss in inference accuracy.
pipelined back-propagation with stale weights is a promising technique that can achieve high throughput while maintaining accuracy, especially when the pipeline is limited to shallow layers.
we can use pipelining to train CNNs with a minimal drop in inference accuracy, but only if we are careful about which layers are pipelined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pipelined back-propagation is feasible for early layers of CNNs, and can be used to accelerate training without significant drop in inference accuracies.
training with stale weights in pipelined back-propagation is feasible and can be used to accelerate training of deep CNNs.
pipelining can be used to train large CNNs on GPUs without significant accuracy degradation.
